{{nihongo|'''Katsurakio Shrine'''|葛木男神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Tosa Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following three deities are currently enshrined. </ref>. {{ill|Shintai|de|Shintai|el|Σίνταϊ|es|Shintai|fa|شین‌تای|fi|Shintai|fr|Shintai|hr|Shintai|id|Shintai|ja|神体|jv|Shintai|ko|신체 (신토)|mk|Шинтаи|pl|Go-shintai|pt|Shintai|ru|Синтай (синтоизм)|simple|Shintai|sr|Шинтаи|tr|Shintai|uk|Сінтай (синто)|zh|神體|qid=Q327532}} is said to be a mirror {{Sfn|Meiji Shrine materials|1912}}.
* '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takami Musubi}}''' (Takami Musubi no Kami)
* '''Katsurakio no Okami'' (Katsurakio no Okami)
*: {{ill|Katsuragi Sotsuhiko|Q11620922|qid=Q11620922|lt=Katsuragi Sotsuhiko no Mikoto}}{{Sfn|Katsuragi Otoshi Shrine (National History)}}. This Katsuragi Sotsuhiko is said to be the founder of the {{ill|Katsuragi clan|Q11620908|qid=Q11620908}} of the powerful clan in the Yamato-Katsuragi region (currently {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Nara|af|Nara-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Nara|ar|نارا (محافظة)|az|Nara prefekturası|azb|نارا اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Nara|bat_smg|Naras prefektūra|be|Нара (прэфектура)|bg|Нара (префектура)|bn|নারা প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Nara|cdo|Nara-gâing|ce|Нара (префектура)|ceb|Nara-ken|ckb|پارێزگای نارا|cs|Prefektura Nara|cy|Nara (talaith)|da|Nara-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Nara|eo|Gubernio Nara|es|Prefectura de Nara|et|Nara prefektuur|eu|Nara (prefektura)|fa|استان نارا|fi|Naran prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Nara|frr|Nara (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Nara|gl|Prefectura de Nara|gor|Prefektur Nara|hak|Nara-yen|he|נארה (מחוז)|hr|Nara (prefektura)|hu|Nara prefektúra|hy|Նարա (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Nara|ilo|Prepektura ti Nara|it|Prefettura di Nara|ja|奈良県|jv|Préfèktur Nara|ka|ნარის პრეფექტურა|kk|Нара (префектура)|km|ណារ៉ា(ខេត្ត)|ko|나라현|la|Naraënsis|lt|Naros prefektūra|lv|Naras prefektūra|mk|Нара (префектура)|mni|ꯅꯥꯔꯥ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|नारा प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Nara|my|နာရခရိုင်|nl|Nara (prefectuur)|no|Nara (prefektur)|os|Нарæ (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Nara|pl|Prefektura Nara|pnb|ضلع نارا|pt|Nara (prefeitura)|ro|Prefectura Nara|ru|Нара (префектура)|sco|Nara Prefectur|sd|نارا پريفيڪچر|se|Nara prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Nara|si|නාරා ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Nara Prefecture|sk|Nara (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Nara|sr|Префектура Нара|su|Nara Prefecture|sv|Nara prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Nara|ta|நாரா மாநிலம்|tg|Префектураи Нара|th|จังหวัดนาระ|tl|Prepektura ng Nara|tok|ma Nala|tr|Nara (prefektörlük)|tt|Нара (префектура)|uk|Префектура Нара|ur|نارا پریفیکچر|vi|Nara (tỉnh)|war|Nara (prefektura)|wuu|奈良县|zh|奈良县|zh_classical|奈良縣|zh_min_nan|Nara-koān|zh_yue|奈良縣|qid=Q131287}}{{ill|Gose, Nara|Q847334|qid=Q847334}} area) {{Sfn|Katsuragi Otoshi Shrine (National History)}}.
* '''Katsurakihime no Okami''
*: Katsuragi Sotsuhikohiko no Mikoto {{Sfn|Katsuragi Otoshi Shrine (National History)}}. Became the enshrined deity of the jointly enshrined Katsuragi Shrine {{Sfn|Katsuragio Shrine (National History)}}.

=== About the enshrined deity ===
In historical materials from {{ill|Early modern period|an|Edat Moderna|ar|الحقبة الحديثة المبكرة|ast|Edá Moderna|az|Erkən modern dövr|bar|Friae Neizeid|be|Ранні Новы час|bn|প্রারম্ভিক আধুনিক যুগ|br|Amzerioù modern|ca|Edat moderna|cs|Raný novověk|cy|Cyfnod Modern Cynnar|da|Tidlig moderne tid|de|Frühe Neuzeit|el|Πρώιμη νεότερη περίοδος|eo|Frua moderna epoko|es|Edad Moderna|et|Varauusaeg|eu|Aro Modernoa|fa|دوران نوین آغازین|fi|Varhaismoderni|fr|Époque moderne|gl|Idade Moderna|gn|Ára Ko'ãgagua|he|העת החדשה המוקדמת|hi|प्रारंभिक आधुनिक काल|hu|Korai újkor|ia|Etate Moderne|id|Periode modern awal|io|Modern-epoko|it|Età moderna|ja|近世|kbp|Alɩwaatʊ kɩfatʊ (Période moderne)|ko|근세|ku|Destpêka Dema Nûjen|kw|Oos Arnowydh A-Varr|lb|Neizäit|lfn|Eda moderna|li|Vreugmodernen Tied|lij|Etæ Modèrna|lld|Storia moderna|lmo|Età Modèrna|lo|ຍຸກ​ສະ​ໄຫມ​ຕົ້ນ​|lt|Naujieji amžiai|lv|Agrīnie jaunie laiki|mg|Andro Vaovao|mk|Ран нов век|new|प्रारम्भिक आधुनिक काल|nl|Vroegmoderne tijd|nn|Tidleg nytid|no|Tidlig moderne tid|oc|Edat Modèrna|pap|Edad Moderno|pcd|Histoère modérne|pl|Nowożytność|ps|لومړۍ معاصره دوره|pt|Idade Moderna|rm|Temp modern tempriv|ro|Epoca modernă timpurie|ru|Раннее Новое время|sc|Edade moderna|sh|Rani novi vijek|simple|Early modern period|sq|Periudha e hershme moderne|sr|Rani novi vek|stq|Eermodärne Tied|sv|Tidigmoderna tiden|th|สมัยใหม่ตอนต้น|tl|Makabagong kasaysayan|tr|Yeni Çağ|tt|Иртә яңа заман|uk|Ранній новий період|vi|Thời kỳ cận đại|vls|Nieuwn tyd|wuu|近世|yi|נייע צייט|zh|近世|zh_yue|近代史|qid=Q5308718}} onward, there are theories that the deity enshrined at Katsuragi Otsuhiko Shrine is {{ill|Katsuragi Sotsuhiko|Q11620922|qid=Q11620922}}, and that it is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takōsan Reimyo}}. Currently, the deity enshrined is based on both these theories.
* Katsuragi Sotsuhiko Theory
*: "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|de|Shinsen Shōjiroku|fr|Shinsen shōjiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録|ko|신찬성씨록|ru|Синсэн сёдзироку|zh|新撰姓氏錄|qid=Q1045362}}" <ref group="Hara">'Newly Selected Names and Names' Roku, Izumi Province Emperor Betsu Fushishinjo. </ref>, this theory is based on the fact that Fushiomi (Fushiji) is a descendant of Katsuragi Sotsuhiko. It is said that the name of the place ``Fushida'' came about because this Fushi clan lived in the area and enshrined Katsuragi Sotsuhiko as their ancestral deity.
* The theory of a spirit born from a high emperor*: "Newly Selected Names and Names Roku" <ref group="Hara"> "Newly Selected Names and Names Roku" Kawachi Kunijinbetsu Tenjin Naojo Katsuragi. </ref><ref group="Hara">``Newly Selected Names and Names Record'', Yamato Province, Jinbetsu, Tenjin, Katsuragi Death Note. A theory based on </ref> that Nao Katsuragi and Insun Katsuragi are the descendants of Takamitama no Mikoto (Takamitama no Mikoto/Takanosei no Mikoto). It is assumed that the shrine names that appear in the early modern period, such as ``Takamusubi Daimyo Jingu,'' ``Takatsuma Daimyo Jingu,'' and ``Takamusubisha,'' originate from this enshrined deity, and it is also assumed that the Katsuragi clan ({{ill|Katsuragi clan|Q11620908|qid=Q11620908}}) is the Hosai clan. However, there is also a theory that the {{ill|Inbe clan|Q8189229|qid=Q8189229}}, who are also descendants of spirits born to the Emperor, are the Hosai clan {{Sfn|Katsuragio Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987}}. Furthermore, since the spirit born to the Emperor is a deity without sex, the ``Shikinai-sha Investigation Report'' considers the Katsuragi Sotsuhiko theory to be the most likely {{Sfn|Katsuragi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987}}

In addition to the above, there is also an Itsubun of the Tosa Province Fudoki {{ill|Lost literary work|Q1585442|qid=Q1585442}}<ref group="Hara" name="Tsuchiza Okami-no-ko">'Gajijikabutsu'. </ref>So,{{Quotation|There is a shrine inside the county house in Tsuchisa. The name of God is ``The Life of the Milky Way.'' If you go down the southern road, there is a shrine. The name of the god is ``Jyokawa Hime no Mikoto'', the daughter of the god of the Milky Way. The god of the Milky Way is Seri, the son of the great god of Tsuchisa. |Isbun (original text in Chinese) from ``Tosa no Kuni Fudoki'' quoted in ``Gagaji Questions and Answers'' <ref group="Hara" name="Toshisa Okami noko"/><ref>The new text is based on ``New Edition of Japanese Classical Literature Complete Works 5 Fudoki'', Shogakukan, 2003 (Japan Knowledge Edition), p. 514. </ref>}}As such, there is a {{jal of Tsuchisa Okami ({{ill|Tosa Shrine|Q704890|qid=Q704890}} enshrined deity) in {{ill|Gunga (Japan)|Q11643230|qid=Q11643230|lt=gunge}} of {{ill|Tosa District, Kōchi|es|Distrito de Tosa|fr|District de Tosa|id|Distrik Tosa, Kōchi|it|Distretto di Tosa|ja|土佐郡|ko|도사군|pl|Powiat Tosa|uk|Повіт Тоса|zh|土佐郡|qid=Q1132134}}. ink|Mikogami|Q352176}}There appears to be a shrine that enshrines ``Amakawa no Mikoto'' (Amakawa no Mikoto), and there appears to be a shrine that enshrines ``Kiyokawa Hime no Mikoto'' (Kiyokawa Hime no Mikoto), the daughter god of Tenga no Mikoto, on the road south of Gunge.<ref name="Fudoki"/>. Tenga no Mikoto and Jokawa Hime no Mikoto are gods that are not mentioned in other documents, but as mentioned later, the Tosa County family is presumed to be near the former enshrinement site of Katsuragi Otoko Shrine, so there is a theory that they are compared to Katsuragi Otokogami and Katsuragi Maki no Kami <ref name="History of Kochi Prefecture"> History of Kochi Prefecture, Yamakawa Publishing, 2001, pp. 47-48. </ref><ref name="Fudoki"> "{{ill|Nihon Koten Bungaku Zenshū|Q11507506|qid=Q11507506|lt=New Edition of Complete Works of Japanese Classical Literature}} 5 Fudoki" Shogakukan, 2003 ({{ill|JapanKnowledge|Q11309996|qid=Q11309996}} edition), pp. 513-514. </ref>. The Tosa County family is thought to have been established by incorporating the shrine of Tenga no Mikoto, which had existed for a long time.<ref name="Fudōki"/><ref name="History of Kochi Prefecture"/>, and it is presumed that this area was the center of {{ill|Tosa Kunizo|Q21653737|qid=Q21653737}} (Tosa Kunizo), a powerful clan, before the establishment of Tosa County.<ref name="History of Kochi Prefecture"/> This Tosa Kunizo is said to be descended from the {{ill|Kamo no Ason clan|ja|賀茂朝臣氏|qid=Q122979457}}, which descends from the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Miwa clan}} in the Yamato-Katsuragi region.<ref name="History of Kochi Prefecture"/>It is also related to our company's name, "Katsuragi." In that case, it is very likely that the original enshrined deity was '''{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mishio Takahikone no Mikoto}}'', the ancestor of Tsusa Kunizo, who is enshrined in Takagamo in Katsuragi.<ref> {{ill|Toshio Hōga|Q11452691|qid=Q11452691}}' Old shrines and priests in central Tosa], Koju Ki no Bosama, 1998. </ref>. However, even though Katsuragi Ogami was the son of Tsuchisa Okami in ancient times, there is no known ritual relationship between the current Tosa Shrine and Katsuragi Otoko Shrine.

=== History ===
[[File:Katsurakihime-jinja (old place).JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|Katsurakihime-jinja old place}}]]
The date of establishment of both Katsuragi Otoshi Shrine and Katsuragi Maki Shrine is unknown. According to legend, both shrines were originally enshrined in the same precincts to the southeast of the current shrine area (currently south of the village of Shimotsuke), but Katsuragi Shrine was moved to the southeast ({{Coord|33|34|55.01|N|133|36|27.87|E|region:JP-39_type:landm ark|name=Old location of Katsuragi Shrine}}), Katsuragi Otoko Shrine also moved to its current location in the northwest to avoid the rising waters of the {{ill|Kokubu River (Kouchi)|Q11420533|qid=Q11420533}}. In addition, it is an itbun of "Tosa Province Fudoki" <ref group="original"> "Shaku Nihongi" volume 12 (Shogi 8) Hitotsubushijinjo or volume 15 (Shogi 11) Tosa no Okami Ichito Shinyu Emperor's article is included in the "Tosa Province Fudoki" Isbun. According to </ref>, the Tosa County family was located 4 ri (approximately 2 kilometers) east of Tsuchisa Takagamo Taisha Shrine ({{ill|Tosa Shrine|Q704890|qid=Q704890}}), but it is assumed that the location was near the former enshrinement area, {{Sfn|Katsuragio Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987}}.{{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長
